SPX.label: S&P 500
SPX.source: Polygon I:SPX 8/26 settled close, re-derived this run. Effectively unchanged, down 1.58 points, as the whole tape stood still waiting for Nvidia. Reuters had the closing arithmetic at -0.02%. Down 0.42% over the past week. NOT ATH - 1.58% below the 8/13/26 record close 7798.99 (record high 7816.70 the same day). S&P futures were +0.4% on the Reuters global wrap at 01:59 GMT

NDX.label: Nasdaq 100
NDX.source: Polygon I:NDX 8/26 settled close, up 15 points, the only US large-cap benchmark to finish green and by the narrowest possible margin. Still -0.68% on the week. NOT ATH - 4.68% below the 6/2/26 record close 30660.60 (record high 30762.20 on 6/3). Nasdaq futures were +0.8% overnight per the Reuters wrap, so the Nvidia bid is landing in futures rather than in yesterday's cash session

SOX.label: Philly Semis
SOX.source: Polygon I:SOX 8/26 settled close, the best US index on the day at +0.20% and the second straight gain, though still -1.08% over the week. NOT ATH and still 20.66% below the 6/22/26 record close 14634.72 - the semiconductor complex sits more than 20% off its own record on the morning after its largest constituent reported 106% revenue growth. That gap is the single most useful number on this page. European tech (.SX8P) was +1.3% overnight on the Nvidia read-through

DJI.label: Dow 30
DJI.source: Polygon I:DJI 8/26 settled close, -113.52 points, the weakest of the four and the only one to break a streak - it had risen three straight. Flat on the week at +0.00%. NOT ATH - 1.63% below the 8/5/26 record close 54349.12 (record high 54744.33). The old-economy index lagging on a day the AI complex held is the reverse of the rotation pattern seen earlier in August

VIX.label: VIX
VIX.source: Polygon I:VIX 8/26 settled close, -1.55%, going INTO the largest single-stock binary event of the quarter. The unsettled 8/27 bar prints 14.89 and is deliberately NOT used as the tile value. VIX3M settled 17.99 and VXN, the Nasdaq-100 vol index, settled 21.42, -1.70% - a front-to-3M ratio of 0.85, so the term structure was in NORMAL CONTANGO through the event. Reuters put the implied Nvidia move at 5.4% against 6.5% ahead of the May print: the options market charged LESS for this print than the last one, and was right

US10Y.label: US 10Y
US10Y.source: TradingEconomics dedicated instrument page at 06:16, +1.9bp, with the prior settle reconstructed from TE's own displayed change. Note the intra-morning drift: the Reuters global wrap at 01:59 GMT had the 10Y at 4.644%, -2bp, so yields have backed up roughly 3bp since the Asian session as the Nvidia bid built. Up 6bp on the month and 46bp on the year. Today brings $44B of 7-year supply at 1:00 PM

US2Y.label: US 2Y
US2Y.source: TradingEconomics dedicated page, +1.8bp, prior settle reconstructed from TE's own change field. 2s10s sits at 43.2bp, a whisker flatter than yesterday. The 30Y is 5.19%, +1.6bp, still the highest since 2007 on TE's own read. Yesterday's $70B 5-year auction (CUSIP 91282CRK9) cleared at 4.393% with a 2.37 bid-to-cover, taken from TreasuryDirect's own results file rather than a calendar aggregator. Front-end yields are RISING while cut odds sit at zero - the curve is pricing a Fed that is done easing, not one about to start

WTI.label: WTI Crude
WTI.source: Reuters oil desk at 08:00 GMT, -$1.40, a FIFTH consecutive session of losses. Named cause per Reuters: Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani travels to Tehran TODAY to relaunch mediation on the Strait of Hormuz. SOURCE CONFLICT DISCLOSED: TradingEconomics' WTI page read 82.2199 at 04:18, essentially unchanged and $1.39 higher. Both feeds reconstruct to the same 82.23 prior settle, so the disagreement is in the live print. Two independent Reuters snapshots against one CFD feed - the wire wins and TE oil is logged DEGRADED for this run

BRENT.label: Brent Crude
BRENT.source: Reuters oil desk at 08:00 GMT, -$1.36, a FOURTH consecutive decline. Corroborated in direction by a second and separate Reuters desk - the global markets wrap at 01:59 GMT had Brent $86.8, -1.1%. TradingEconomics read 88.278, +0.50%, at 07:19 and is the outlier, logged DEGRADED. Counter-evidence held in the same window: UKMTO Warning 121-26 was issued around 00:54 GMT after a tanker was struck by a projectile near Khasab, Oman. The market is trading the diplomacy, not the projectile

GOLD.label: Gold
GOLD.source: TradingEconomics quote, -$1.50, against a prior settle reconstructed from TE's own change field and INDEPENDENTLY corroborated by the Reuters global wrap, which had gold near $4,598, +0.1%, implying the same base near 4593. Flagged for the record: Polygon's C:XAUUSD 8/26 daily bar closed 4623.43, roughly $30 higher, almost certainly a bar-boundary difference rather than a price disagreement - the two-source agreement is preferred. Still +14.0% on the month. NOT a record - 16.10% below the 1/28/26 record close 5510.73 (record high 5596.68 the same day), verified against two years of daily bars

BTC.label: Bitcoin
BTC.source: Coinbase public spot at 11:20 UTC against Polygon's settled 8/26 close of 79026.18, re-derived this run (Polygon crypto live and minute endpoints both return 403 - entitlement absent, not retried). Up 14.06% on the week and 24.07% on the month; Reuters attributes the metals-and-crypto August surge to dollar debasement trades following the Treasury's bond-market intervention last week. NOT a record - 36.64% below the 10/6/25 record close 124720.09

EURJPY.label: EUR/JPY
EURJPY.source: TradingEconomics quote against Polygon's C:EURJPY settled 8/26 close of 185.612, re-derived this run. Unchanged to four decimal places - TE's own page prints the change as 0%. USD/JPY is 159.470, +0.10%, and the dollar index is 99.240, +0.08%. The yen is marginally softer against the dollar and pinned against the euro: no funding stress signature whatsoever, which matters because a yen-carry unwind is the standard tail risk attached to a big AI-equity move

AUDJPY.label: AUD/JPY
AUDJPY.source: TradingEconomics quote against Polygon's C:AUDJPY settled 8/26 close of 114.357. Both carry crosses are flat-to-higher, the opposite of a funding squeeze. Worth holding alongside it: the ASX 200 fell about 1% overnight on a hot Australian inflation print that raised RBA hike risk, so AUD strength here is a rate-differential story rather than a risk-appetite story. EUR/USD 1.16395, -0.10%; AUD/USD 0.71802, +0.14%
